title.en: Volume 301 Biographies 88: Ne Qin, Fu Heng, Fu Ling An, Fu Long An, Fu Long An, Feng Shenjilun, Fu Chang An
title.raw: 卷301 列傳八十八 讷亲 傅恒 福灵安 福隆安 福隆安 丰绅济伦 福长安

sentences.zh: 列傳八十八

translations.literal: Biographies 88
translations.idiomatic: Biography 88

sentences.zh: 訥親傅恆子福靈安福隆安福隆安子丰紳濟倫福長安

translations.literal: Ne Qin, Fu Heng, sons Fu Ling'an and Fu Long'an, Fu Long'an's son Feng Shenjilun, and Fu Chang'an
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin; Fu Heng; Fu Ling'an and Fu Long'an; Feng Shenjilun, son of Fu Long'an; and Fu Chang'an

sentences.zh: 訥親，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，額亦都曾孫。

translations.literal: Ne Qin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and a great-grandson of E Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin, of the Niohuru clan, came from the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner and was a great-grandson of E Yidu.

sentences.zh: 父尹德，附見其父遏必隆傳，訥親其次子。

translations.literal: His father was Yin De; see the biography of his father Ebilun—Ne Qin was the second son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin De is treated in the biography of Ebilun; Ne Qin was Ebilun's second son.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，襲公爵，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he inherited the dukedom and was appointed an attendant minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 he succeeded to the dukedom and was made an attendant minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 十年，授鑾儀使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed director of the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became director of the imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，命在辦理軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he was assigned to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十三年，世宗疾大漸，訥親預顧命。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Yongzheng Emperor's illness grew grave, Ne Qin was named to the deathbed council.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, as the Yongzheng Emperor lay critically ill, Ne Qin was included among those entrusted at the deathbed.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，莊親王允祿、果親王允禮、鄂爾泰、張廷玉輔政，號「總理王大臣」。

translations.literal: When the Qianlong Emperor ascended the throne, Prince Zhuang Yunlu, Prince Guo Yunli, Ortai, and Zhang Tingyu assisted in government and were styled the "Grand Ministers in Charge of General Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: After Qianlong took the throne, Prince Zhuang Yunlu, Prince Guo Yunli, Ortai, and Zhang Tingyu formed the regency styled the Grand Ministers in Charge of General Affairs.

sentences.zh: 授訥親鑲白旗滿洲都統、領侍衛內大臣，協辦總理事務。

translations.literal: Ne Qin was appointed Manchu commander of the Bordered White Banner and chief grand minister of the imperial bodyguard, and was to assist in general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin was made Manchu commander of the Bordered White Banner and chief grand minister of the imperial bodyguard, with a role in the general administration.

sentences.zh: 十二月，敕獎訥親勤慎，因推孝昭仁皇后外家恩，進一等公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict praised Ne Qin's diligence and prudence; in recognition of favor owed to the maternal kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren, he was advanced to a first-class duke.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month an edict commended Ne Qin's diligence; citing the debt owed Empress Xiaozhaoren's family, the court raised him to a first-class duke.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，遷鑲黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to be Manchu commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he became Manchu commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十一月，莊親王等請罷總理事務，訥親授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Prince Zhuang and others asked that the office of general affairs be abolished; Ne Qin was appointed a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Prince Zhuang and the others petitioned to end the general-affairs regency, and Ne Qin was named a Grand Council minister.

sentences.zh: 敘勞，加拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: His service was recorded in reward, and he was granted a hereditary tuosalahafan rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received a hereditary cavalry commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，領戶部三庫。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he took charge of the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he assumed charge of the Board of Revenue's three treasuries.

sentences.zh: 九月，命協辦戶部。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was ordered to assist in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was assigned to assist the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督李衛劾總河硃藻詐欺貪虐，命訥親與尚書孫嘉淦勘讞，藻坐流。

translations.literal: Zhili governor-general Li Wei impeached the director-general of waterways Zhu Zao for fraud, oppression, and greed; Ne Qin and Minister Sun Jiaheng were ordered to investigate and pass judgment, and Zhu was sentenced to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhili governor-general Li Wei accused waterways director Zhu Zao of fraud and brutal corruption, Ne Qin and Minister Sun Jiaheng were sent to try the case; Zhu was banished.

sentences.zh: 訥親因與嘉淦條上永定河南北岸建築閘壩諸事。

translations.literal: Ne Qin thereupon joined Jiaheng in submitting itemized proposals on building sluices and dams along the north and south banks of the Yongding River.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin then joined Jiaheng in a detailed memorial on sluices and dams along both banks of the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was given the additional title Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was made Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 訥親貴戚勳舊，少侍禁近，受世宗知，以為可大用。

translations.literal: Ne Qin was a noble kinsman of meritorious stock who from youth had attended at the inner palace; the Yongzheng Emperor knew him and judged that he could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: A noble kinsman of an old military house, Ne Qin had served near the throne from youth; Yongzheng knew him well and believed he was fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 迨高宗，恩眷尤厚。

translations.literal: Under the Qianlong Emperor favor toward him was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong his favor was deeper still.

sentences.zh: 訥親勤敏當上意，尤以廉介自敕，人不敢干以私。

translations.literal: Ne Qin was diligent and quick to suit the emperor's mind, and above all disciplined himself in integrity so that no one dared approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and alert to the emperor's wishes, he above all held himself to strict integrity, and no one dared press him with private business.

sentences.zh: 其居第巨獒縛扉側，絕無車馬跡。

translations.literal: At his residence a huge mastiff was tied beside the door, and there was never a trace of carriage or horse.
translations.idiomatic: A great mastiff was tied beside the door of his house, and no carriage ever came near.

sentences.zh: 然以早貴，意氣驕溢，治事務刻深。

translations.literal: Yet because he had risen early to high rank, his spirit was proud and overflowing, and in handling affairs he was invariably harsh and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having risen young to high rank, he grew proud and overbearing, and in government he was relentlessly severe.

sentences.zh: 左都御史劉統勳疏論訥親領事過多，任事過銳。

translations.literal: Left censor-in-chief Liu Tongxun memorialized that Ne Qin took charge of too many matters and pursued his duties with excessive sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Left censor-in-chief Liu Tongxun memorialized that Ne Qin held too many portfolios and drove his work too hard.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「訥親為尚書，模棱推諉，固所不可，但治事未當，亦所不免，朕時時戒毋自滿。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "As a minister, Ne Qin must not be evasive and shirk responsibility—that is certainly unacceptable—but that his handling of affairs is not always right is also unavoidable; I constantly warn him not to grow complacent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "As a minister Ne Qin must not hedge and pass the buck—that will not do—but it is also inevitable that his handling of affairs will sometimes miss the mark; I am always warning him not to grow complacent.

sentences.zh: 今見此奏，益當自勉。

translations.literal: Now that I see this memorial, he should strive all the more."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this memorial, he should redouble his efforts."

sentences.zh: 」語詳統勳傳。

translations.literal: " The full text is given in the biography of Tongxun.
translations.idiomatic: " The full exchange is recorded in Liu Tongxun's biography.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，命訥親閱河南、江南、山東諸省營伍，並勘海塘、河工。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year Ne Qin was ordered to inspect the garrisons of Henan, Jiangnan, and Shandong and also to survey the seawalls and river works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he was sent to inspect garrisons in Henan, Jiangnan, and Shandong and to survey seawalls and river works.

sentences.zh: 時直隸天津、河間二府方以災治賑，令順道先往察覈。

translations.literal: At that time Tianjin and Hejian prefectures in Zhili were administering disaster relief; he was ordered to go by the way and investigate first.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin and Hejian in Zhili were then under disaster relief, and he was told to go there first on his route.

sentences.zh: 疏請展賑一月，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to extend relief by one month, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to extend relief by a month, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 訥親使事既蕆，分疏上陳，其勘諸省營伍，言：「遍閱三省督撫、河漕、提鎮為標者十七，優絀互見。

translations.literal: When Ne Qin's mission was finished he submitted separate memorials; on his inspection of the provincial garrisons he wrote: "Having reviewed the whole of the three provinces, I took as benchmarks seventeen governors-general, governors, grain-transport and river officials, and regional commanders—merit and demerit were mixed.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour was done he filed separate reports; on the garrisons he wrote: "Across the three provinces I reviewed seventeen governors, grain-transport and river officials, and regional commanders as benchmarks—some did well, some poorly.

sentences.zh: 惟河南南陽、江南蘇松水師二鎮最劣。

translations.literal: Only the two naval commands of Nanyang in Henan and Susong in Jiangnan were the worst.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Nanyang command in Henan and the Susong naval command in Jiangnan were the worst.

sentences.zh: 請下部覈賞罰。

translations.literal: I ask that the ministries verify and impose rewards and punishments."
translations.idiomatic: I ask the ministries to verify this and fix rewards and punishments."

sentences.zh: 」其勘江、浙海塘，言：「舊日浙江潮自蜀山中小亹出入，近海寧為北大亹，近蕭山為南大亹，漲沙寬闊，為杭州、紹興二府保障。

translations.literal: On his survey of the Jiangsu and Zhejiang seawalls he wrote: "Formerly the tide in Zhejiang entered and left through the middle channel at Shushan; near Haining was the northern great channel and near Xiaoshan the southern great channel, with broad accretions of sand that protected the two prefectures of Hangzhou and Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiangsu and Zhejiang seawalls he reported: "Once the Zhejiang tide ran in and out through the middle channel at Shushan; near Haining lay the northern great channel and near Xiaoshan the southern, with wide sand bars that sheltered Hangzhou and Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 迨中小亹漸湮，潮趨蜀山北，震盪為患。

translations.literal: When the middle channel gradually silted up, the tide turned north of Shushan and its surging became a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: As the middle channel silted up, the tide swung north of Shushan and began to pound the coast.

sentences.zh: 若濬中小亹故道，減大亹潮力，上下塘工悉可安堵；

translations.literal: If the old course of the middle channel were dredged, the force of the great channels' tide would be reduced and the seawall works above and below could all be secured;
translations.idiomatic: If the middle channel were dredged open again, the great channels' force would ease and the seawalls up and down the coast could be made secure;

sentences.zh: 即中小亹未可遽复，則當擇險要多為坦坡，木石戧壩，俾撇水積淤資以御潮。

translations.literal: even if the middle channel could not quickly be restored, then at critical points many gentle slopes and timber-and-stone spur dikes should be built so that water might be deflected and silt accumulate to help resist the tide.
translations.idiomatic: and even if the middle channel could not soon be reopened, gentle slopes and timber-and-stone spur dikes should be built at the danger points to deflect the water, let silt build up, and hold back the tide.

sentences.zh: 至諸處柴塘，停沙阻水，無煩議改石工。

translations.literal: As for the brushwood seawalls in various places, they detain sand and obstruct water; there is no need to discuss converting them to stone works.
translations.idiomatic: As for the brushwood seawalls elsewhere, they trap sand and slow the water; there is no need to debate converting them to stone.

sentences.zh: 入江南境，地平而潮緩，華亭舊塘堅緻，寶山新塘尺度參差，工作又不中程。

translations.literal: Entering Jiangnan, the land is level and the tide slow; the old seawall at Huating is solid and fine, but the new wall at Baoshan is irregular in scale and the workmanship also fails to meet standard.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan the land is flat and the tide gentle; Huating's old seawall is sound, but Baoshan's new wall varies in scale and the work does not meet specification.

sentences.zh: 金山、奉賢、南匯、上海皆土塘，距海稍遠，所司守護如法，當無他虞。

translations.literal: Jinshan, Fengxian, Nanhui, and Shanghai all have earthen seawalls somewhat farther from the sea; if the offices in charge guard them according to rule, there should be no other worry.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshan, Fengxian, Nanhui, and Shanghai all rely on earthen walls set somewhat back from the sea; if their keepers maintain them properly, they should give no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 」其勘洪澤湖，請濬鹽河俾通江，疏串場河俾達海，並停天然二壩、高堰下游二堤。

translations.literal: On his survey of Hongze Lake he asked to dredge the salt transport canal so it might reach the Yangzi, to clear the Chuanchang canal so it might reach the sea, and to halt work on the two natural dams and the two dikes below Gaoyan.
translations.idiomatic: On Hongze Lake he proposed dredging the salt canal to the Yangzi, clearing the Chuanchang canal to the sea, and suspending work on the two natural dams and the two dikes below Gaoyan.

sentences.zh: 其勘南旺湖，請以湖中涸地貸貧民耕稼。

translations.literal: On his survey of Nanwang Lake he asked that the dried land in the lake be lent to poor people for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanwang Lake he proposed lending reclaimed lake bed to the poor for farming.

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「各直省政事，督撫下司道，司道下州縣，州縣官惟以簿書錢穀為事，戶口貧富、土地肥瘠、物產豐嗇、民情向背、風俗美惡、以及山川原隰、橋樑道路，皆漫置不省。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: "In the administration of each province, governors-general and governors stand above intendants and circuit intendants, and they above prefects and magistrates; yet prefectural and county officials concern themselves only with ledgers and taxes. Household wealth and poverty, whether land is fertile or poor, whether products are abundant or scarce, whether the people's disposition is favorable or hostile, whether customs are good or bad, and even mountains, rivers, plains, marshes, bridges, and roads—all are carelessly set aside and never examined.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "In each province governors rule through intendants and they through magistrates, yet county officials care only for paperwork and taxes. Population, land, produce, popular sentiment, custom, terrain, bridges, and roads—all go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 官但有條教，民惟責納賦，浮文常多，實意殊少。

translations.literal: Officials have only regulations; the people are charged only to pay taxes—empty documents are many, real intent very little.
translations.idiomatic: Officials issue rules; the people pay taxes—form fills the files, substance scarcely appears.

sentences.zh: 請敕各直省督撫，令州縣官遍歷境內，何事當興舉，何事當整飭，行之有無治效，以實報長官，長官即是為殿最，以實達朝廷。

translations.literal: I ask that each province's governor-general and governor be commanded to order prefectural and county officials to travel through their whole jurisdictions, reporting in substance to their superiors what should be undertaken and what rectified, and whether measures taken have had effect; the superiors should then use this as the basis for ranking performance and report in substance to the court.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors order magistrates to tour their districts, report what should be built or reformed, and show results; superiors should rank them on that basis and report truthfully to the throne.

sentences.zh: 似亦崇實效、去虛文、飭吏治、厚民生之一端也。

translations.literal: This would seem to be one means of honoring real results, removing empty documents, tightening official discipline, and enriching the people's livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: That would be one way to prize results over paperwork, tighten rule, and improve people's lives."

sentences.zh: 」皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were sent to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he was made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 五月，授保和殿大學士，仍兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony, while still retaining the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was made grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony while keeping the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，命如山西會巡撫愛必達讞萬全民張世祿、安邑民張遠等挾眾抗官狀，論如律。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to Shanxi to join Governor Aibidai in trying the case of Wanquan commoner Zhang Shilu, Anyi commoner Zhang Yuan, and others who had gathered crowds to resist officials; judgment followed the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year he went to Shanxi with Governor Aibidai to try Zhang Shilu of Wanquan, Zhang Yuan of Anyi, and others who had led mobs against the magistrates; they were sentenced by law.

sentences.zh: 愛必達及總兵羅俊、蒲州知府硃發等皆坐譴黜。

translations.literal: Aibidai, regional commander Luo Jun, Puzhou prefect Zhu Fa, and others were all punished with reprimand and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Aibidai, regional commander Luo Jun, Puzhou prefect Zhu Fa, and others were all reprimanded and removed.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，命如浙江會大學士高斌覆勘巡撫常安貪婪狀，未至，高斌鞫得常安實受賕，訥親與共奏，論如律。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was ordered to Zhejiang to join Grand Secretary Gao Bin in re-investigating Governor Chang An's greed; before Ne Qin arrived, Gao Bin had already established that Chang had in fact taken bribes, and Ne Qin joined him in memorializing; judgment followed the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was sent to Zhejiang with Grand Secretary Gao Bin to reinvestigate Governor Chang An's corruption; before Ne Qin arrived, Gao Bin had already proved the bribes, and together they memorialized for sentencing under law.

sentences.zh: 三月，復命如山東會巡撫阿里袞治賑。

translations.literal: In the third month he was again ordered to Shandong to join Governor Aligun in administering disaster relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was again sent to Shandong with Governor Aligun to oversee relief.

sentences.zh: 時大金川土司莎羅奔攻革布什咱土司犯邊，上命川陝總督張廣泗討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Greater Jinchuan chieftain Slob Dpon attacked the Gelebusizan chieftain and violated the border; the emperor ordered Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general Zhang Guangsi to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Jinchuan chieftain Slob Dpon had attacked Gelebusizan and raided the frontier, and the emperor ordered Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general Zhang Guangsi against him.

sentences.zh: 大金川地絕險，阻山為石壘，名曰碉，師進攻弗克。

translations.literal: Greater Jinchuan country was utterly perilous; blocking the mountains they built stone ramparts called diao, and the army's attacks could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Jinchuan was desperately rugged; the tribes walled the mountains in stone forts called diao, and the army could not break them.

sentences.zh: 四月，召訥親還京師，授經略大臣，率禁旅出視師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Ne Qin was recalled to the capital, appointed commissioner-general, and sent out at the head of the imperial guard to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ne Qin was recalled, made commissioner-general, and sent out with the imperial guard to take command.

sentences.zh: 六月，訥親至軍，下令期三日克噶拉依，噶拉依者，莎羅奔結寨地也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Ne Qin reached the army and issued an order to take Galai within three days—Galai being the place where Slob Dpon had fortified his camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he reached the front and ordered Galai, Slob Dpon's stronghold, taken within three days.

sentences.zh: 師循色爾力石梁而下，攻碉未即克，署總兵任舉勇敢善戰，為諸軍先，沒於陣。

translations.literal: The army advanced down the Serli stone ridge to attack the diao but could not take them at once; acting regional commander Ren Ju, brave and skilled in battle, led all the forces and fell in the field.
translations.idiomatic: The troops moved down the Serli stone ridge against the forts without immediate success; acting regional commander Ren Ju, bold in battle, led the van and was killed.

sentences.zh: 訥親為氣奪，乃議督諸軍築碉，與敵共險，為持久。

translations.literal: Ne Qin's spirit was broken, and he then proposed to supervise the army in building diao, sharing the perilous ground with the enemy for a prolonged contest.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin lost heart and proposed that the army build diao of its own and settle into a long contest on the same deadly ground as the enemy.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上重失任舉，又以築碉非計，手詔戒訥親，因時度勢，以為進止。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor deeply regretted the loss of Ren Ju and also held that building diao was no plan; he personally drafted an edict warning Ne Qin to gauge the times and circumstances in deciding advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived the emperor mourned Ren Ju deeply and judged that building diao was folly; he wrote Ne Qin in his own hand to weigh time and circumstance before advancing or holding back.

sentences.zh: 訥親與廣泗合疏言：「天時地利皆賊得其長，我兵無機可乘。

translations.literal: Ne Qin and Zhang Guangsi jointly memorialized: "Heaven's seasons and earth's advantages all fall where the enemy excels; our troops have no opening to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin and Zhang Guangsi jointly reported: "Season and terrain favor the enemy; our troops find no opening.

sentences.zh: 冬春間當減兵駐守，明歲加調精銳三萬，於四月進剿，足以成功，至遲亦不逾秋令。

translations.literal: Between winter and spring we should reduce the army to garrison duty; next year add thirty thousand picked troops and advance in the fourth month—enough to succeed, and at the latest not beyond autumn.
translations.idiomatic: We should cut forces to garrison strength through winter and spring, add thirty thousand elite troops next year, and strike in the fourth month—enough to win, and at latest by autumn."

sentences.zh: 」訥親又別疏言：「來歲增兵，計需費數百萬。

translations.literal: Ne Qin also separately memorialized: "To increase troops next year will require several million in expense.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin also wrote separately: "Reinforcements next year will cost millions.

sentences.zh: 若俟二三年後有機可乘，亦未可定。

translations.literal: If we wait two or three years for an opening, that too cannot be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Whether an opening will appear in two or three years is equally uncertain."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上諭曰：「卿等身在戎行，目擊情狀，不能確有成算，游移兩可。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor instructed: "You are yourselves in the army and see the situation with your own eyes, yet cannot settle on a firm plan and waver between two positions.
translations.idiomatic: When the reports arrived the emperor replied: "You are on the spot and see the fighting yourselves, yet you offer no firm plan and hedge both ways.

sentences.zh: 朕於數千里外，何從遙度？

translations.literal: I, several thousand li away—how am I to judge from afar?
translations.idiomatic: How can I judge from a thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 我師至四萬，彼止三千餘，何以彼應我則有餘，我攻彼則不足？

translations.literal: Our army reaches forty thousand while they have only a little over three thousand—why is it that they have surplus in meeting us, yet we are insufficient in attacking them?
translations.idiomatic: We field forty thousand men against barely three thousand—why do they have strength to spare when we meet them, yet we fall short when we attack?

sentences.zh: 卿等當審定應攻應罷，毋為兩歧語。

translations.literal: You should determine whether to attack or to cease, and not speak in two different ways."
translations.idiomatic: Decide whether to fight or withdraw, and do not speak with two tongues."

sentences.zh: 」上知訥親不足辦敵，諭軍機大臣議召訥親還；

translations.literal: The emperor knew Ne Qin was unequal to dealing with the enemy and instructed the Grand Council ministers to discuss recalling him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Ne Qin could not handle the enemy and told the Grand Council to discuss recalling him;

sentences.zh: 又念大金川非大敵，重臣視師，無功而還，傷國體，為四夷姍笑。

translations.literal: yet he also reflected that Greater Jinchuan was no great foe, and that for a high minister to oversee the army and return without achievement would wound the state's dignity and invite the four barbarians' mockery.
translations.idiomatic: yet Greater Jinchuan was no great power, and for a senior minister to command in person and return empty-handed would shame the state and invite the border peoples' scorn.

sentences.zh: 密以諭訥親，冀激奮克敵。

translations.literal: He secretly informed Ne Qin in the hope of stirring him to rouse himself and overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Ne Qin on, hoping to stir him to victory.

sentences.zh: 居數月，師雖有小胜，卒未得尺寸地。

translations.literal: After several months, though the army had small victories, in the end it gained not a foot of ground.
translations.idiomatic: After several months the army won minor skirmishes but never took an inch of ground.

sentences.zh: 訥親惟請還京面對，乃召訥親及廣泗詣京師，以岳鍾琪攝經略，傅爾丹攝川陝總督，復遣尚書班第同治軍事。

translations.literal: Ne Qin only asked to return to the capital for an audience; Ne Qin and Zhang Guangsi were then summoned to the capital, Yue Zhongqi was made acting commissioner-general, Fu Erdan acting Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, and Minister Ban Di was again sent to manage military affairs jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin could only ask to return for an audience; he and Zhang Guangsi were recalled, Yue Zhongqi was made acting commissioner-general, Fu Erdan acting governor-general of Sichuan-Shaanxi, and Minister Ban Di was again sent to the front.

sentences.zh: 尋奪訥親官，令自具鞍馬，從討噶爾丹贖罪，逮廣泗。

translations.literal: Soon Ne Qin's office was stripped; he was ordered to provide his own saddle and horse and follow the campaign against the Dzungars to redeem his guilt, and Zhang Guangsi was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ne Qin was stripped of rank and told to furnish his own horse and follow the Dzungar campaign to atone; Zhang Guangsi was arrested.

sentences.zh: 九月，命大學士傅恆代為經略，別遣侍衛富成逮訥親，責置對，並令富成錄訥親舉止言語以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Grand Secretary Fu Heng was appointed commissioner-general in his stead; a separate order sent guard Fu Cheng to arrest Ne Qin and bring him to answer charges, and Fu Cheng was also commanded to record Ne Qin's conduct and speech for report.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Grand Secretary Fu Heng replaced him as commissioner-general; guard Fu Cheng was sent to seize Ne Qin for interrogation and to report his words and conduct.

sentences.zh: 上前後手詔罪訥親恆數千百言，略謂：「訥親受命總戎，乖張畏縮。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly drafted by his own hand edicts condemning Ne Qin, running to thousands of words, saying in summary: "Ne Qin received command of the army yet was perverse and timid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote thousands of words in his own hand condemning Ne Qin, saying in essence: "Ne Qin took command of the army yet was obstinate and timid.

sentences.zh: 疏言軍夜攻碉，自帳中望見火光，知未嘗臨敵。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said that when the army attacked the diao by night, he watched the firelight from his tent and thus knew he had never faced the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that when the army attacked the forts by night he watched the flames from his tent—proof he never faced the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又言督軍攻阿利山，既回營，我軍數十人各鳥獸散。

translations.literal: He also said that when he supervised the army in attacking Ali Mountain and had already returned to camp, several tens of our troops scattered each like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that after he led the attack on Ali Mountain and returned to camp, dozens of our men scattered like frightened animals.

sentences.zh: 知偶臨敵，又先士卒退。

translations.literal: Thus it is known that even when he occasionally faced the enemy, he withdrew ahead of the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: So even when he did approach the fighting, he withdrew before the troops.

sentences.zh: 富成疏訥親語'金川事大難，不可輕舉，此言不敢入奏'。

translations.literal: Fu Cheng memorialized Ne Qin's words: 'The Jinchuan affair is greatly difficult and must not be lightly undertaken—this statement I dare not enter in a memorial.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Cheng reported Ne Qin's words: "The Jinchuan war is desperately hard and must not be undertaken lightly—I dare not say this in a memorial."

sentences.zh: 訥親受恩久，何事不可言？

translations.literal: Ne Qin has long received favor—what matter may he not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin has enjoyed favor for years—what could he not say to the throne?

sentences.zh: 如固不能克，當實陳請罷兵。

translations.literal: If he truly could not overcome the foe, he should have stated it plainly and asked to cease the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: If he truly could not win, he should have asked plainly to stop the war.

sentences.zh: 乃事敗欲以不可輕舉歸過朝廷，狡詐出意外。

translations.literal: Yet when affairs failed he wished to lay the blame on the court with 'must not be lightly undertaken'—cunning beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, after defeat he would blame the court with "must not be lightly undertaken"—cunning beyond belief.

sentences.zh: 又值續調兵過，輒言'此皆我罪，令如許滿洲兵受苦'。

translations.literal: Again, when additional troops were being transferred past, he would say, 'All this is my fault, causing so many Manchu soldiers to suffer.'
translations.idiomatic: When fresh troops marched past he would say, "This is all my fault, making so many Manchu soldiers suffer."

sentences.zh: 滿洲兵聞調，鼓舞振躍，志切同仇。

translations.literal: When Manchu soldiers heard of transfer, they were inspired and leapt up, their will keen to share the enemy's fate.
translations.idiomatic: The Manchu troops, hearing they were called up, were eager and burning to fight.

sentences.zh: 訥親以為受苦，實嫉他人成功，搖眾心，不顧國事。

translations.literal: Ne Qin spoke of suffering, but in truth he envied others' success, shook the army's heart, and disregarded the state's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin called it suffering, but in truth he envied others' success, undermined morale, and ignored the state's interest.

sentences.zh: 孤恩藐法，罪不可逭。

translations.literal: Ungrateful toward favor and contemptuous of law, his crime cannot be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ungrateful and lawless, his crime admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: 十月，諭「訥親先世以軍功封二等公，為孝昭仁皇后戚屬，供職勤慎，進一等公。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict stated: "Ne Qin's forebears were enfeoffed as second-class dukes for military merit; as kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren he served diligently and was advanced to first-class duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict ruled: "Ne Qin's house had been enfeoffed as a second-class duke for military merit; as kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren he served diligently and was raised to first-class duke.

sentences.zh: 獲罪，應仍以二等公俾其兄策楞襲爵」。

translations.literal: Having incurred guilt, the title should still revert to second-class duke for his elder brother Celeng to inherit."
translations.idiomatic: Having fallen, the rank should revert to second-class duke for his elder brother Celeng to inherit."

sentences.zh: 訥親恃上恩，尚冀入見上自解，上复迭降手詔，謂：「軍旅事重，平日治事詳慎，操守潔清，舉不足言。

translations.literal: Ne Qin relied on imperial favor and still hoped to see the emperor and explain himself; the emperor again repeatedly sent personal edicts, saying: "Military affairs are weighty; that in ordinary administration he was careful in detail and pure in conduct is not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin still counted on imperial favor and hoped to explain himself in audience; the emperor again wrote in his own hand: "War is grave business—his careful administration and clean conduct in peacetime count for nothing.

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「訥親小心謹密，而方寸一壞，天奪其魄，雖欲倖免而不能。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ne Qin was cautious and close in small matters, yet once his inner resolve was ruined Heaven took his spirit—even wishing to escape he could not."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Ne Qin was careful in small things, but once his heart failed Heaven took his wits—he could not escape even if he wished."

sentences.zh: 」十二月，廣泗既誅，上封遏必隆遺刀授侍衛鄂實，監訥親還軍，誅以警眾。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, after Zhang Guangsi had been executed, the emperor sealed Ebilun's heirloom blade and gave it to guard E Shi to supervise Ne Qin's return to the army and execute him to warn the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, after Zhang Guangsi was executed, the emperor sealed Ebilun's heirloom blade and gave it to guard E Shi to escort Ne Qin back to the army and execute him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，上命傅恆班師，复諭鄂實即途中行法。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year the emperor ordered Fu Heng to withdraw the army and again instructed E Shi to carry out the sentence on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year the emperor ordered Fu Heng to withdraw and told E Shi to execute Ne Qin on the way.

sentences.zh: 是月戊寅，鄂實監訥親行至班攔山，聞後命，遂誅訥親。

translations.literal: On day wuyin of that month E Shi, supervising Ne Qin's march, reached Banlan Mountain; hearing the later order, he then executed Ne Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day that month E Shi, escorting Ne Qin, reached Banlan Mountain; on receiving the final order he executed him.

sentences.zh: 傅恆，字春和，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，孝賢純皇后弟也。

translations.literal: Fu Heng, style Chunhe, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and younger brother of Empress Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng, courtesy name Chunhe, of the Fuca clan, came from the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner and was the younger brother of Empress Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 父李榮保，附見其父米思翰傳。

translations.literal: His father was Li Rongbao; see the biography of his father Misanhan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Rongbao is treated in the biography of Misanhan.

sentences.zh: 傅恆自侍衛洊擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Fu Heng was promoted step by step from guard to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng rose from the guards to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年六月，命在軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Qianlong he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Qianlong 10 he joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，孝賢純皇后從上南巡，還至德州崩，傅恆扈行，典喪儀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year Empress Xiaoxian accompanied the emperor on the southern tour; returning, she died at Dezhou; Fu Heng attended on the journey and presided over the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year Empress Xiaoxian accompanied the southern tour; she died at Dezhou on the return, and Fu Heng, who had attended her, directed the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 四月，敕獎其勤恪，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict praised his diligence and granted him the additional title Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict commended his diligence and made him Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時訥親視師金川，解尚書阿克敦協辦大學士以授傅恆，並兼領吏部。

translations.literal: At that time Ne Qin was overseeing the army in Jinchuan; Minister Agedun was relieved of his post as associate grand secretary and it was given to Fu Heng, who also retained charge of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: While Ne Qin commanded in Jinchuan, Minister Agedun was replaced as associate grand secretary by Fu Heng, who also kept the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 訥親既無功，九月，命傅恆暫管川陝總督，經略軍務。

translations.literal: After Ne Qin achieved nothing, in the ninth month Fu Heng was ordered to act as Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general and take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ne Qin failed, Fu Heng was made acting governor-general of Sichuan-Shaanxi and commissioner-general in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 尋授保和殿大學士，發京師及諸行省滿、漢兵三萬五千，以部庫及諸行省銀四百萬供軍儲，又出內帑十萬備犒賞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; thirty-five thousand Manchu and Han troops were dispatched from the capital and the provinces, four million taels from the ministry treasuries and the provinces were supplied for army stores, and one hundred thousand from the privy purse was issued for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; thirty-five thousand Manchu and Han troops were mobilized from the capital and provinces, four million taels allocated for supplies, and one hundred thousand from the privy purse for rewards.

sentences.zh: 十一月，師行，上詣堂子告察，遣皇子及大學士來保等送至良鄉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the army marched; the emperor went to the tangse to announce the campaign, and sent princes and Grand Secretary Laibao and others to escort them as far as Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the army marched; the emperor prayed at the tangse for success, and princes and Grand Secretary Laibao escorted the column to Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 傅恆既行，上日降手詔褒勉。

translations.literal: After Fu Heng had set out, the emperor daily sent personal edicts of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Heng marched, the emperor wrote him daily with praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 傅恆道陝西，言驛政不修誤軍興，上命協辦大學士尚書尹繼善攝陝西總督，主饋運。

translations.literal: Fu Heng, passing through Shaanxi, reported that neglected courier service was hindering the campaign; the emperor ordered Associate Grand Secretary and Minister Yin Jishan to act as Shaanxi governor-general and take charge of transport.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Shaanxi, Fu Heng reported that bad courier service was crippling the campaign; the emperor put Associate Grand Secretary Yin Jishan in charge of Shaanxi transport as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 入四川境，馬不給，上又命尹繼善往來川、陝督察。

translations.literal: Entering Sichuan, horses were insufficient; the emperor again ordered Yin Jishan to travel between Sichuan and Shaanxi to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan horses ran short, and Yin Jishan was again ordered to shuttle between Sichuan and Shaanxi to supervise.

sentences.zh: 旋以傅恆師行甚速，紀律嚴明，命議敘，部議加太子太傅，特命加太保。

translations.literal: Soon, because Fu Heng's army marched very swiftly with strict discipline, he was ordered recorded for reward; the ministry proposed adding Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and he was specially ordered made Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Heng's column proved swift and disciplined, the ministries proposed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the emperor specially made him Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不允，發京師及山西、湖北馬七千佐軍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was not permitted; seven thousand horses from the capital, Shanxi, and Hubei were dispatched to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: He declined but was overruled, and seven thousand horses were sent from the capital, Shanxi, and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 傅恆發成都，經天赦山，雪後道險，步行七十里至驛。

translations.literal: Fu Heng set out from Chengdu, passed Tianshe Mountain; after snow the road was perilous, and he walked seventy li to the post station.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Chengdu he crossed Tianshe Mountain; after snow the trail was deadly, and he walked seventy li to the next station.

sentences.zh: 上聞，賜雙眼孔雀翎，复固辭。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he bestowed double-eyed peacock feathers; Fu Heng again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor gave him double-eyed peacock feathers; he declined again.

sentences.zh: 初，小金川土舍良爾吉間其兄澤旺於莎羅奔，奪其印，即烝於嫂阿扣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lesser Jinchuan tusi Lang Erji had slandered his elder brother Zewang to Slob Dpon, seized his seal, and at once took his sister-in-law A Kou in levirate union.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Lang Erji had turned Slob Dpon against his brother Zewang, seized Zewang's seal, and taken his sister-in-law A Kou.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔之犯邊也，良爾吉實從之，後詐降為賊諜。

translations.literal: When Slob Dpon violated the border, Lang Erji had in fact followed him; later he feigned surrender and served as a spy for the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Erji had joined Slob Dpon's border raids and later feigned surrender to spy for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 張廣泗入奸民王秋言，使領蠻兵，我師舉動，賊輒知之。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangsi took in the traitor Wang Qiu and had him lead barbarian troops, so that whenever our army moved, the enemy at once knew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi employed the traitor Wang Qiu to lead tribal auxiliaries, so the enemy always knew our moves.

sentences.zh: 傅恆途中疏請誅良爾吉等，將至軍，使副將馬良柱招良爾吉來迎，至邦噶山，正其罪，並阿扣、王秋悉誅之。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized on the road asking to execute Lang Erji and others; nearing the army he had vice commander Ma Liangzhu summon Lang Erji to welcome him; at Bangga Mountain he judged their crimes and executed A Kou and Wang Qiu as well.
translations.idiomatic: En route Fu Heng asked to execute Lang Erji; near the front he had vice commander Ma Liangzhu lure Lang Erji to Bangga Mountain, tried him, and executed A Kou and Wang Qiu as well.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上褒傅恆明斷，命拜前賜雙眼孔雀翎，毋更固辭。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor praised Fu Heng's clear decisiveness and ordered him to accept the previously bestowed double-eyed peacock feathers and not decline again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his decisiveness and ordered him to accept the peacock feathers without further refusal.

sentences.zh: 十月，至卡撒，以屯軍地狹隘，與賊相望，且雜處番民巿肆中，乃相度移舊壘前，令總兵冶大雄監營壘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Kasa; because the garrison ground was narrow and faced the enemy across a short distance, and was moreover mixed among tribal markets, he surveyed the ground and moved forward of the old camp, ordering regional commander Ye Daxiong to supervise the fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Kasa; the camp was cramped, face to face with the enemy amid tribal markets, so he moved the lines forward and put regional commander Ye Daxiong in charge of building new works.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，上疏言：「臣至軍，察用兵始末：當紀山進討之始，馬良柱轉戰而前，逾沃日收小金川直抵丹噶，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year he memorialized: "Having reached the army, I have examined the campaign from start to finish: when the advance began from Jishan, Ma Liangzhu fought his way forward, crossed Wo Ri, took Lesser Jinchuan, and pressed straight to Danga—his edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year he wrote: "At the army I reviewed the whole campaign: when the advance began from Jishan, Ma Liangzhu fought through Wo Ri, took Lesser Jinchuan, and drove to Danga with fierce momentum.

sentences.zh: 彼時張廣泗若速進師，賊備未嚴，殄滅尚易；

translations.literal: If at that time Zhang Guangsi had advanced the army swiftly, the enemy's preparations were not yet strict and extermination would still have been easy;
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhang Guangsi pressed on then, before the enemy was ready, victory would have been easy;

sentences.zh: 乃坐失事機，宋宗璋宿留於雜穀，許應虎敗衄於的郊，賊得盡據險要，增碉備禦。

translations.literal: instead the opportunity was lost, Song Zongzhang lingered at Zagu, Xu Yinghu was defeated at Dijiao, and the enemy came to hold all the strategic points and added diao for defense.
translations.idiomatic: instead Song Zongzhang stalled at Zagu, Xu Yinghu was beaten at Dijiao, and the enemy seized every strong point and threw up diao.

sentences.zh: 訥親初至，督戰甚急，任舉敗沒，銳挫氣索，軍無鬥志，一以軍事委張廣泗。

translations.literal: When Ne Qin first arrived he pressed battle very urgently; Ren Ju was defeated and killed, keen edge and spirit were broken, the army had no will to fight, and he wholly entrusted military affairs to Zhang Guangsi.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin at first drove the fighting hard; Ren Ju's death broke morale, and he handed everything to Zhang Guangsi.

sentences.zh: 廣泗又為奸人所愚，專主攻碉。

translations.literal: Guangsi was again deceived by traitors and devoted himself solely to attacking diao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi, duped by traitors, fixated on storming the diao.

sentences.zh: 先後殺傷數千人，匿不以聞。

translations.literal: Several thousand were killed and wounded in succession, and he concealed it without reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands died in these assaults, which he never reported.

sentences.zh: 臣惟攻碉最為下策，槍砲不能洞堅壁，於賊無所傷。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that attacking diao is the worst stratagem: muskets and cannon cannot pierce solid walls and do the enemy no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking diao is the worst strategy: muskets and cannon cannot breach stone walls and hurt no one inside.

sentences.zh: 賊不過數人，自暗擊明，槍不虛發。

translations.literal: The enemy are only a few men, striking from darkness at those in the light; not a shot is wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few defenders fire from cover into the open, and every shot tells.

sentences.zh: 是我惟攻石，而賊實攻人。

translations.literal: Thus we attack only stone while the enemy in truth attack men.
translations.idiomatic: We batter stone while they kill men.

sentences.zh: 賊於碉外為濠，兵不能越，賊伏其中，自下擊上。

translations.literal: Outside the diao the enemy dig moats that troops cannot cross; the enemy lie hidden within and strike from below upward.
translations.idiomatic: They dig moats our men cannot cross and shoot downward from ambush.

sentences.zh: 其碉銳立，高於浮屠，建作甚捷，數日可成，旋缺旋補。

translations.literal: Their diao stand sharp and tall, higher than pagodas; they are built very swiftly, finished in days, and as soon as one is broken another is patched.
translations.idiomatic: The forts rise higher than pagodas, go up in days, and are rebuilt as fast as we smash them.

sentences.zh: 且眾心甚固，碉盡碎而不去，砲方過而復起。

translations.literal: Moreover their hearts are very firm: though the diao are utterly shattered they do not leave; the cannon have barely passed and they rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Their will is iron: though a fort is shattered they do not flee, and as our guns move on they rebuild.

sentences.zh: 客主勞佚，形勢迥殊，攻一碉難於克一城。

translations.literal: Guest and host, toil and ease, the situation utterly different—taking one diao is harder than taking a city.
translations.idiomatic: We labor, they rest; taking one diao is harder than storming a city.

sentences.zh: 即臣所駐卡撒，左右山巔三百餘碉，計日以攻，非數年不能盡。

translations.literal: Even at Kasa where your servant is stationed, on the peaks to left and right are more than three hundred diao; counting by days of assault, several years would not suffice to finish them.
translations.idiomatic: Around Kasa alone more than three hundred diao crown the ridges; at this pace years would not clear them.

sentences.zh: 且得一碉輒傷數十百人，得不償失。

translations.literal: Moreover, for each diao taken several tens or hundreds are wounded—the gain does not repay the loss.
translations.idiomatic: Each fort costs scores or hundreds of lives—the price is not worth paying.

sentences.zh: 兵法，攻堅則瑕者堅，攻瑕則堅者瑕。

translations.literal: In the art of war, attack what is strong and what is weak becomes strong; attack what is weak and what is strong becomes weak.
translations.idiomatic: As the strategists say: strike the strong and the weak grow strong; strike the weak and the strong grow weak.

sentences.zh: 惟使賊失所恃，我兵乃可用其所長。

translations.literal: Only by making the enemy lose what they rely on can our troops then use their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Only by depriving them of their advantage can our troops fight as they are meant to.

sentences.zh: 擬俟諸軍大集，分道而進。

translations.literal: I propose to wait until the armies are fully gathered and advance by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to wait until the armies assemble and advance on several routes.

sentences.zh: 別選銳師，旁探間道，裹糧直入，逾碉勿攻，繞出其後。

translations.literal: Separately select elite troops to probe side paths, carry rations and plunge straight in, pass the diao without attacking, and circle behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Pick elite columns to find side paths, march in with rations, bypass the diao without fighting, and take the enemy from behind.

sentences.zh: 番眾不多，外備既密，內守必虛。

translations.literal: The tribesmen are not numerous; outer defenses being dense, inner defense must be empty.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes are few; with their strength on the perimeter, the interior must be hollow.

sentences.zh: 我兵既自捷徑深入，守者各懷內顧，人無固志，均可不攻自潰。

translations.literal: Once our troops have entered deep by swift paths, each defender will look inward with concern, men will have no firm will, and all can collapse without being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Once our men cut in by fast routes, the garrisons will look to their rear, lose heart, and collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 卡撒為進噶拉依正道，嶺高溝窄，臣當親任其難。

translations.literal: Kasa is the main road to Galai; ridges are high and gullies narrow—your servant will personally undertake the hard part.
translations.idiomatic: Kasa is the main road to Galai, with high ridges and narrow defiles—I will take that hard road myself.

sentences.zh: 黨壩隘險，亦幾同卡撒，酌益新軍。

translations.literal: Dangba is narrow and perilous, almost the same as Kasa; I will consider adding fresh troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dangba is nearly as tight as Kasa; I will reinforce that column.

sentences.zh: 兩道並進，直搗巢穴，取其渠魁。

translations.literal: The two routes will advance together, strike straight at the nest, and seize the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns will strike the nest together and take the chiefs.

sentences.zh: 期四月間奏捷。

translations.literal: I expect to report victory within the fourth month."
translations.idiomatic: I expect victory by the fourth month."

sentences.zh: 」上以金川非大敵，勞師兩載，誅大臣，失良將，內不懌。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Jinchuan was no great enemy, that the army had labored two years, that ministers had been executed and good generals lost, was inwardly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had never regarded Jinchuan as a great foe, was inwardly troubled after two years of war, executed ministers, and lost generals.

sentences.zh: 及是聞其地險難下，益不欲竟其事，遂以孝聖憲皇后諭命班師，而傅恆方督總兵哈攀龍、哈尚德等攻下數碉。

translations.literal: When he now heard that the ground was perilous and hard to subdue, he was all the more unwilling to see the affair through; he therefore ordered withdrawal by the Empress Dowager Xiaosheng's command, while Fu Heng was just then supervising regional commanders Ha Panlong, Ha Shangde, and others in taking several diao.
translations.idiomatic: Learning how hard the country was, he was even less willing to continue and ordered withdrawal on the Empress Dowager Xiaosheng's advice—just as Fu Heng was taking several diao under Ha Panlong and Ha Shangde.

sentences.zh: 上以金川水土惡，賜傅恆人蓡三斤，並及諸將有差，屢詔召傅恆還。

translations.literal: Because Jinchuan's water and soil were malign, the emperor gave Fu Heng three jin of ginseng and likewise the generals in varying amounts, and repeatedly ordered Fu Heng recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jinchuan's climate was harsh, he sent Fu Heng three jin of ginseng and gifts to the generals, and repeatedly ordered him home.

sentences.zh: 又以孝聖憲皇后諭封一等忠勇公，賜寶石頂、四團龍補服。

translations.literal: Again by the Empress Dowager Xiaosheng's command he was enfeoffed as first-class Loyal and Brave Duke, and given a jeweled hat finial and four-round-dragon surcoat.
translations.idiomatic: By the empress dowager's command he was made first-class Loyal and Brave Duke with a jeweled finial and four-dragon surcoat.

sentences.zh: 傅恆奏言：「金川事一誤，今復輕率蕆事，賊焰愈張。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized: "The Jinchuan affair was once mishandled; now to end it lightly again will make the enemy's flame blaze higher.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng wrote: "Jinchuan was mishandled once; to quit lightly now will only embolden the enemy.

sentences.zh: 眾土司皆罹其毒，邊宇將無寧日。

translations.literal: All the tusi will suffer their poison, and the borderlands will know no day of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Every tusi will suffer, and the frontier will never know peace.

sentences.zh: 審度形勢，賊碉非盡當道，其巢皆老弱，我兵且戰且前，自昔嶺中峰直抵噶拉依，破竹建瓴，功在垂成，棄之可惜。

translations.literal: Judging the situation, the enemy's diao do not all block the road; their nests are all old and weak; our troops fight as they advance, and from Xiling Peak straight to Galai it is like splitting bamboo or pouring from a height—the achievement hangs on the verge of completion, and to abandon it would be a pity.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's forts do not all block the road; their nests hold only the old and weak; our men are fighting forward from Xiling Peak straight to Galai like splitting bamboo—victory is at hand, and to abandon it would be a waste.

sentences.zh: 且臣受詔出師，若不掃穴擒渠，何顏返命？

translations.literal: Moreover, your servant received an edict to take the field; if I do not sweep the nest and seize the ringleader, with what face can I return to report?"
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to campaign; if I do not root them out and take their chief, how can I return?"

sentences.zh: 」並力辭封賞，上不允，手詔謂：「匈奴未滅，無以家為，乃驃姚武人銳往之概。

translations.literal: He also firmly declined rewards; the emperor would not agree and wrote by his own hand: "While the Xiongnu are not destroyed, one cannot make a home—that is the bold forward spirit of a warrior like Huo Qubing.
translations.idiomatic: He also refused the honors; the emperor would not hear of it and wrote: "While the Xiongnu are not destroyed one cannot make a home—that is the spirit of Huo Qubing.

sentences.zh: 大學士抒誠贊化，豈與兜鍪閫帥爭一日之績？

translations.literal: A grand secretary who expresses sincerity in aiding transformation—how should he vie with helmeted commanders for a single day's merit?"
translations.idiomatic: A grand secretary who aids the throne in civil rule—why should he vie with field commanders for a day's glory?"

sentences.zh: 」反复累數千言，复賜詩喻指。

translations.literal: Again and again he wrote several thousand words, and also bestowed a poem to make his meaning clear.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thousands of words in reply and also sent a poem to make his meaning plain.

sentences.zh: 時傅恆及提督岳鍾琪決策深入，莎羅奔遣頭人乞降，傅恆令自縛詣軍門。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Heng and regional commander-in-chief Yue Zhongqi decided on a deep advance; Slob Dpon sent headmen to beg surrender, and Fu Heng ordered them to bind themselves and come to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng and regional commander-in-chief Yue Zhongqi then decided on a deep thrust; Slob Dpon sent headmen to sue for peace, and Fu Heng ordered them bound and brought to camp.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔复介綽斯甲等詣岳鍾琪乞貸死，鍾琪親入勒烏圍，挈莎羅奔及其子郎卡詣軍門。

translations.literal: Slob Dpon again had Chuosi and others go to Yue Zhongqi to beg that their lives be spared; Zhongqi personally entered Lewuwei and brought Slob Dpon and his son Langka to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Slob Dpon then sent Chuosi and others to Yue Zhongqi to beg for their lives; Zhongqi entered Lewuwei in person and brought Slob Dpon and his son Langka to camp.

sentences.zh: 語詳鍾琪傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in full in the biography of Zhongqi.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in Yue Zhongqi's biography.

sentences.zh: 傅恆遂受莎羅奔父子降，莎羅奔等焚香作樂，誓六事：無犯鄰比諸番，反其侵地，供役視諸土司，執獻諸酋抗我師者，還所掠內地民馬，納軍械槍砲，乃承製赦其罪。

translations.literal: Fu Heng then accepted the surrender of Slob Dpon and his son; Slob Dpon and the others burned incense and made music, swearing six things: not to violate neighboring tribes, to return invaded lands, to supply labor like other tusi, to seize and hand over chiefs who had resisted our army, to return inland people and horses they had plundered, and to surrender military weapons, muskets, and cannon—only then did he receive an imperial pardon of their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng accepted their surrender; they burned incense and swore six terms: no raids on neighbors, return of seized lands, labor like other tusi, delivery of chiefs who had fought us, return of plundered subjects and horses, surrender of arms—then an imperial pardon followed.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔獻​​佛像一、白金萬，傅恆卻其金，莎羅奔請以金為傅恆建祠。

translations.literal: Slob Dpon presented one Buddhist image and ten thousand taels of white silver; Fu Heng refused the silver, and Slob Dpon asked to use the silver to build a shrine to Fu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Slob Dpon offered an image and ten thousand taels of silver; Fu Heng refused the silver, and Slob Dpon asked to build a shrine in his honor instead.

sentences.zh: 翌日，傅恆率師還。

translations.literal: The next day Fu Heng led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fu Heng withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 上優詔嘉獎，命用揚古利故事，賜豹尾槍二桿、親軍二名。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict of praise and ordered the precedent of Yangguli applied, bestowing two leopard-tail spears and two personal guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him in a gracious edict and, following the precedent of Yangguli, gave him two leopard-tail spears and two personal guards.

sentences.zh: 三月，師至京師，命皇長子及裕親王等郊迎。

translations.literal: In the third month the army reached the capital; the heir apparent and Prince Yu and others were ordered to welcome them in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army reached the capital; the heir apparent and Prince Yu were sent to welcome them outside the city.

sentences.zh: 上御殿受賀，行飲至禮。

translations.literal: The emperor took the hall to receive congratulations and performed the ritual of drinking to the army's return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received congratulations in court and held the ritual feast for the returning army.

sentences.zh: 傅恆疏辭四團龍補服，上命服以入朝，復命用額亦都、佟國維故事，建宗祠，祀曾祖哈什屯以下，並追予李榮保諡，賜第東安門內，以詩落其成。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized declining the four-round-dragon surcoat; the emperor ordered him to wear it when entering court, and again ordered the precedents of E Yidu and Tong Guowei applied—a ancestral hall was built, sacrificing from his great-grandfather Hashitun downward, and Li Rongbao was posthumously given a posthumous title; a residence inside Dong'an Gate was bestowed, and the emperor composed a poem on its completion.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng declined the four-dragon surcoat; the emperor made him wear it at court and, following the precedents of E Yidu and Tong Guowei, ordered an ancestral hall for Hashitun and his descendants, posthumous honors for Li Rongbao, and a mansion inside Dong'an Gate, which the emperor marked with a poem at its completion.

sentences.zh: 十九年，準噶爾內亂，諸部台吉多內附。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Dzungars fell into internal disorder and many taiji of the tribes submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Dzungars fell into civil war and many tribal taiji submitted.

sentences.zh: 上將用兵，諮廷臣，惟傅恆贊其議。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to use force and consulted the court; only Fu Heng approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned war he consulted the court; only Fu Heng supported it.

sentences.zh: 二十年，師克伊犁，俘達瓦齊以歸，諭再封一等公，傅恆固辭，至泣下，乃允之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the army took Yili and brought Dawachi back captive; an edict again enfeoffed him as first-class duke; Fu Heng firmly declined until he wept, and only then was it allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Yili fell and Dawachi was brought back captive; the emperor offered to make him a first-class duke again; Fu Heng wept and refused until the emperor yielded.

sentences.zh: 尋圖功臣像紫光閣，上親制贊，仍以為冠，舉蕭何不戰居首功為比。

translations.literal: Soon the meritorious ministers' portraits were painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor; the emperor personally composed encomia and still placed him first, comparing him to Xiao He, who without fighting held the highest merit.
translations.idiomatic: His portrait was soon painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor with an imperial encomium placing him first, compared to Xiao He, who won the highest merit without fighting.

sentences.zh: 二十一年四月，將軍策楞追捕阿睦爾撒納未獲，上命傅恆出視師，赴額林哈畢爾噶，集蒙古諸台吉飭軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year General Celeng pursued Amursana without capturing him; the emperor ordered Fu Heng out to oversee the army, go to Elinhabirga, and assemble the Mongol taiji to regulate military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year General Celeng failed to catch Amursana; Fu Heng was sent to Elinhabirga to oversee the army and rally the Mongol taiji.

sentences.zh: 傅恆行日，策楞疏至，已率兵深入，復召傅恆還。

translations.literal: On the day Fu Heng marched, Celeng's memorial arrived saying he had already led the army deep in pursuit, and Fu Heng was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The day Fu Heng set out, Celeng reported that he had already driven deep in pursuit, and Fu Heng was recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，將軍明瑞徵緬甸敗績，二月，授傅恆經略，出督師。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year General Mingrui's Burma expedition met defeat; in the second month Fu Heng was appointed commissioner-general and went out to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, after General Mingrui's defeat in Burma, Fu Heng was made commissioner-general in the second month and sent to command.

sentences.zh: 時阿里袞以副將軍主軍事，上並授阿桂副將軍、舒赫德參贊大臣，命舒赫德先赴雲南，與阿里袞籌畫進軍。

translations.literal: At that time Aligun was deputy commander-in-chief in charge of military affairs; the emperor also appointed Agui deputy commander-in-chief and Shuhede staff minister, ordering Shuhede to go first to Yunnan to plan the advance with Aligun.
translations.idiomatic: Aligun was then deputy commander; Agui was made deputy commander and Shuhede staff minister, with Shuhede sent ahead to Yunnan to plan the advance with Aligun.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，傅恆師行，發京師及滿、蒙兵一萬三千六百人從征，上御太和殿賜敕，賚御用甲胄。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year Fu Heng's army marched; thirteen thousand six hundred Manchu and Mongol troops from the capital were sent on campaign; the emperor took the Hall of Supreme Harmony to bestow his command and granted imperial armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year he marched with thirteen thousand six hundred Manchu and Mongol troops from the capital; the emperor gave him his command in the Hall of Supreme Harmony and imperial armor.

sentences.zh: 四月，至騰越，傅恆決策，師循戛鳩江而進，大兵出江西，取道猛拱、猛養，直搗木梳，水師沿江順流下，水陸相應。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he reached Tengyue; Fu Heng decided that the army should advance along the Jiujiang River, the main force coming out west of the river by way of Menggong and Mengyang to strike straight at Mushu, while the naval force went downstream along the river so that land and water would coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month at Tengyue he decided the main column would follow the Jiujiang west through Menggong and Mengyang to Mushu while the fleet moved downstream in support.

sentences.zh: 偏師出江東取猛密，夾擊老官屯。

translations.literal: A secondary column would come out east of the river to take Mengmi and attack Laoguantun from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: A flanking force east of the river would take Mengmi and pinch Laoguantun.

sentences.zh: 往歲以避瘴，九月後進兵，緬甸得為備。

translations.literal: In past years, to avoid miasma, troops advanced only after the ninth month, and Burma was able to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Past campaigns had waited until after the ninth month to avoid malaria, giving Burma time to prepare.

sentences.zh: 傅恆互議先數十日出不意，攻其未備，水師當具舟。

translations.literal: Fu Heng discussed advancing several tens of days early to take them unawares and strike before they were ready; the naval force must have boats prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng proposed advancing weeks early by surprise and insisted the fleet be ready.

sentences.zh: 上初命阿里袞造舟濟師，阿里袞等言崖險澗窄不宜舟，傍江亦無造舟所。

translations.literal: The emperor at first ordered Aligun to build boats to ferry the army; Aligun and others said the cliffs were perilous, the streams narrow, unsuitable for boats, and that beside the river there was also no place to build them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had first ordered Aligun to build boats; Aligun replied that the cliffs and narrow streams forbade shipping and that there was no boatyard on the river.

sentences.zh: 上又命三泰、傅顯往視，言與阿里袞等同。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Santai and Fu Xian to go inspect; they reported the same as Aligun.
translations.idiomatic: Santai and Fu Xian were sent to inspect and reported the same.

sentences.zh: 及傅恆至軍，諮土司頭人，知蠻暮有山曰翁古多木，旁有地曰野牛壩，野人所居，涼爽無瘴。

translations.literal: When Fu Heng reached the army and consulted tusi headmen, he learned that in Manmu there was a mountain called Wengguduomu and beside it a place called Yeniuba where wild people lived, cool and free of miasma.
translations.idiomatic: At the front Fu Heng learned from tusi headmen of Wengguduomu mountain in Manmu and nearby Yeniuba, a cool hill country without malaria.

sentences.zh: 即地伐木造舟，野人樂受值，執役甚謹。

translations.literal: At that place they felled timber to build boats; the wild people gladly took payment and performed labor very diligently.
translations.idiomatic: There they felled timber and built boats; the hill people worked gladly for pay.

sentences.zh: 傅恆即使傅顯佐蒞事。

translations.literal: Fu Heng at once had Fu Xian assist in overseeing the work.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng put Fu Xian in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 舟成，督滿、漢兵並從行奴僕，更番轉搬。

translations.literal: When the boats were finished, he supervised Manchu and Han troops together with attendant servants in relays to transport goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the boats were ready, Manchu and Han troops and servants relayed supplies along the river.

sentences.zh: 又得茂隆廠附近砲工，令範銅為砲。

translations.literal: He also obtained artillery craftsmen near Maolong Factory and ordered them to cast bronze for cannon.
translations.idiomatic: He also found gun founders near Maolong and had them cast cannon.

sentences.zh: 狀聞，輒降旨嘉獎，為賦造舟行焉。

translations.literal: When reports arrived, edicts of praise were repeatedly issued, and the emperor composed a poem on building the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Each report brought imperial praise, and the emperor wrote a poem on the boat-building.

sentences.zh: 傅恆初議自將九千三百人渡戛鳩而西，師未集，七月，將四千人發騰越。

translations.literal: Fu Heng at first proposed to lead nine thousand three hundred men himself across the Jiujiang westward; the army was not yet gathered, and in the seventh month he sent four thousand from Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng had planned to lead nine thousand three hundred men across the Jiujiang himself; before the army assembled he sent four thousand from Tengyue in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 上以經略自將師寡，促諸軍速集如初議。

translations.literal: Because the commissioner-general was leading in person with too few troops, the emperor urged the armies to gather quickly as originally planned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing the commissioner-general leading with too few men, urged the armies to assemble as planned.

sentences.zh: 八月，傅恆自南蚌趨戛鳩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fu Heng hurried from Nanbang toward the Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fu Heng pushed from Nanbang toward the Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 奏至，上方行圍木蘭，入圍獲狍，畀福隆安以賜傅恆。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was on the Mulan hunt; entering the enclosure he took a roe deer and had Fu Long'an present it as a gift to Fu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived the emperor was hunting at Mulan; he took a roe deer in the enclosure and sent it to Fu Heng through Fu Long'an.

sentences.zh: 傅恆道南底壩至允帽，臨戛鳩江，時猛拱大頭人脫猛烏猛、頭人賀丙等，詣傅恆請降。

translations.literal: Fu Heng passed Nandiba to Yunmao on the Jiujiang; at that time Menggong's great headman Tuomengwumeng, headman He Bing, and others came to Fu Heng to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng reached Yunmao on the Jiujiang by way of Nandiba; Menggong's headmen Tuomengwumeng and He Bing came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師至，脫猛烏猛將夾江諸夷寨頭人來迎，與賀丙具舟。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, Tuomengwumeng brought the headmen of the tribal stockades on both banks of the river to welcome them, and together with He Bing provided boats.
translations.idiomatic: When the army arrived Tuomengwumeng brought the riverine chiefs to welcome them, and he and He Bing supplied boats.

sentences.zh: 傅恆命分兵徐濟，夾江為寨猛拱后土司渾覺亦請降，獻馴象四。

translations.literal: Fu Heng ordered troops to cross in detachments at leisure; stockades were set on both banks of the river; Menggong's queen tusi Hunjue also asked to surrender and presented four tame elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng ferried troops over in detachments and set camps on both banks; Menggong's queen tusi Hunjue also surrendered and gave four tame elephants.

sentences.zh: 上賚三眼孔雀翎，傅恆疏辭。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed triple-eyed peacock feathers; Fu Heng memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him triple-eyed peacock feathers; Fu Heng declined by memorial.

sentences.zh: 師復進，取猛養，破寨四，誅頭人拉匿拉賽。

translations.literal: The army advanced again, took Mengyang, broke four stockades, and executed headman Lanilasai.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced again, took Mengyang, stormed four stockades, and executed headman Lanilasai.

sentences.zh: 設台站，令瑚爾起以七百人駐守。

translations.literal: Relay stations were established and Hu Erqi was ordered to garrison with seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Relay stations were set up and Hu Erqi garrisoned them with seven hundred men.

sentences.zh: 遂至南董幹，攻南準寨，獲頭人木波猛等三十五人。

translations.literal: They then reached Nandonggan, attacked Nanzhun stockade, and captured headman Mubomeng and thirty-five others.
translations.idiomatic: They then reached Nandonggan, took Nanzhun stockade, and captured headman Mubomeng and thirty-five others.

sentences.zh: 進次暮臘，再進次新街。

translations.literal: They advanced next to Mula, then again to Xinjie.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Mula, then advanced again to Xinjie.

sentences.zh: 傅恆自渡戛鳩江，未嘗與緬甸兵戰，刈禾為糧，行二千里不血刃，而士馬觸暑雨多疾病。

translations.literal: From the time Fu Heng crossed the Jiujiang he had not yet fought Burmese troops; they reaped grain for provisions and marched two thousand li without drawing a blade, yet men and horses suffered many illnesses from heat and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Since crossing the Jiujiang Fu Heng had not fought the Burmese; living off the harvest he marched two thousand li without battle, while heat and rain sickened men and horses.

sentences.zh: 會阿桂將萬餘人自虎踞關出野牛壩，造舟畢成，徵廣東、福建水師亦至，乃合軍並進。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Agui led more than ten thousand men out from Hujuguan through Yeniuba; when boat-building was finished and the Guangdong and Fujian naval forces also arrived, the armies united and advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: Agui meanwhile led ten thousand men from Hujuguan through Yeniuba; when the boats were ready and Guangdong and Fujian fleets arrived, the columns united and advanced.

sentences.zh: 哈國興將水師，阿桂、阿里袞將陸師，阿桂出江東，阿里袞出江西。

translations.literal: Ha Guoxing commanded the naval force; Agui and Aligun commanded the land forces—Agui on the river's east bank, Aligun on the west.
translations.idiomatic: Ha Guoxing led the fleet; Agui and Aligun the land forces—Agui east of the river, Aligun west.

sentences.zh: 緬兵壘金沙江兩岸，又以舟師扼江口。

translations.literal: Burmese troops fortified both banks of the Jinsha River and also used a fleet to hold the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese fortified both banks of the Jinsha and blocked the river mouth with boats.

sentences.zh: 阿桂先與緬兵遇，麾步兵發銃矢，又以騎兵陷陣，緬兵潰。

translations.literal: Agui first met Burmese troops, ordered the infantry to fire muskets and arrows, and also used cavalry to break the formation; the Burmese army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Agui met the Burmese first, had infantry fire muskets and arrows and cavalry charge the line, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 哈國興督舟師乘風蹴敵，緬兵舟相擊，死者數千。

translations.literal: Ha Guoxing supervised the fleet to ride the wind and strike the enemy; Burmese boats collided in battle and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Ha Guoxing drove the fleet downwind into the enemy; thousands died as the Burmese boats crashed together.

sentences.zh: 阿里袞亦破西岸緬兵，傅恆以所獲纛進。

translations.literal: Aligun also broke the Burmese on the west bank, and Fu Heng presented the captured banners.
translations.idiomatic: Aligun broke the western Burmese as well, and Fu Heng forwarded the captured banners.

sentences.zh: 上復為賦詩，阿里袞感瘴而病，改將水師，旋卒。

translations.literal: The emperor again composed a poem; Aligun fell ill from miasma, was transferred to command the naval force, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote another poem; Aligun sickened with malaria, took command of the fleet, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，傅恆復進攻老官屯，老官屯在金沙江東，東猛密，西猛墅，北猛拱、猛養，南緬都阿瓦，為水陸通衢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Fu Heng again advanced to attack Laoguantun; Laoguantun lies east of the Jinsha, with Mengmi to the east, Mengshu to the west, Menggong and Mengyang to the north, and the Burmese capital Ava to the south—it is a thoroughfare by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fu Heng attacked Laoguantun, east of the Jinsha between Mengmi and Mengshu, north of Menggong and Mengyang and south of Ava—the junction of land and water routes.

sentences.zh: 緬兵伐木立寨甚固，哈國興督諸軍力攻，未即克。

translations.literal: The Burmese felled timber and built a very solid stockade; Ha Guoxing supervised the armies in fierce assault but could not take it at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese built a stout timber stockade; Ha Guoxing assaulted it hard without immediate success.

sentences.zh: 師破東南木寨，緬兵夜自水寨出，傅恆令海蘭察御之，又令伊勒圖督舟師掩擊，复獲船纛。

translations.literal: The army broke the southeastern timber stockade; at night the Burmese came out from the water stockade; Fu Heng ordered Hailancha to repel them and also ordered Yiletuo to supervise the fleet in a surprise attack, again capturing boat banners.
translations.idiomatic: Our men took the southeastern timber fort; the Burmese sallied from the water fort by night; Fu Heng had Hailancha hold them off and Yiletuo strike by water, capturing more banners.

sentences.zh: 緬兵潛至江岸築壘，又自林箐中出，海蘭察擊之，屢有斬馘。

translations.literal: The Burmese secretly came to the riverbank to build ramparts and also emerged from the forest thickets; Hailancha struck them and repeatedly took heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese built riverbank works and struck from the woods; Hailancha beat them back with repeated kills.

sentences.zh: 師久攻堅，士卒染瘴多物故，水陸軍三萬一千，至是僅存一萬三千。

translations.literal: The army had long assaulted strong positions; many soldiers sickened and died from miasma; of thirty-one thousand land and naval troops, only thirteen thousand now remained.
translations.idiomatic: After long assaults malaria killed many; of thirty-one thousand land and naval troops only thirteen thousand remained.

sentences.zh: 傅恆以入告，上命罷兵，召傅恆還京。

translations.literal: Fu Heng reported this inward; the emperor ordered the campaign halted and Fu Heng recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng reported in; the emperor ordered the war stopped and Fu Heng recalled.

sentences.zh: 傅恆俄亦病，阿桂以聞。

translations.literal: Fu Heng soon fell ill as well, and Agui reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng soon fell ill, which Agui reported.

sentences.zh: 上令即馳驛還，而以軍事付阿桂。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to return immediately by express relay and entrusted military affairs to Agui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him home by express relay and left the army to Agui.

sentences.zh: 會緬甸酋懵駁遣頭人諾爾塔齎蒲葉書乞罷兵，傅恆奏入，上許其行成。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Burmese chief Meng Bo sent headman Nuoerta with a palm-leaf letter begging to cease fighting; Fu Heng memorialized it, and the emperor permitted a truce.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese chief Meng Bo sent Nuoerta with a palm-leaf plea for peace; Fu Heng reported it and the emperor agreed to truce.

sentences.zh: 傅恆附疏言：「用兵之始，眾以為難。

translations.literal: Fu Heng appended a memorial saying: "At the start of the campaign everyone thought it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng added: "When the war began everyone called it hard.

sentences.zh: 臣執意請行，負委任，請從重治罪。

translations.literal: Your servant insisted on going, bore the commission, and asks to be punished severely."
translations.idiomatic: I insisted on going and bore the charge; I ask severe punishment."

sentences.zh: 」上手詔謂：「用兵非得已，如以為非是，朕當首任其過。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote by his own hand: "Using force is unavoidable; if you think it wrong, I should bear the fault first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote: "War is unavoidable; if it was wrong, I should bear the blame first.

sentences.zh: 皇祖時，吳三桂請撤籓，諮於群臣，議撤者惟米思翰、明珠數人。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era, when Wu Sangui asked to surrender his fief, the Grand Emperor consulted the ministers; only Misanhan, Nalan Mingzhu, and a few others favored withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, when Wu Sangui asked to give up his fief, only Misanhan, Nalan Mingzhu, and a few others favored accepting.

sentences.zh: 及三桂反，眾請誅議撤諸臣，皇祖深闢其非。

translations.literal: When San Gui rebelled, many asked that the ministers who had favored withdrawal be executed; the Grand Emperor strongly rejected this.
